reply.title: Squashing with the Logistic Sigmoid
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural activations, we often need to take any real number from negative to positive infinity and squash it neatly into a range between zero and one. A linear scale fails because it grows without bound. Instead, we can use the logistic function, which maps inputs smoothly across an S-shaped curve.

As the input x moves far to the left, the denominator grows large and the output approaches zero. As x moves far to the right, the exponential term shrinks and the output approaches one. The steepness parameter k controls how fast the transition happens, while the midpoint x0 shifts the center of the curve.

By examining the curve and its tangent slope at a given point, we can see exactly how sensitive the output is to changes in the input. This smooth squashing mechanism prevents saturation issues and lets systems make probabilistic decisions.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid function maps any real number into the range between zero and one. Adjust the steepness $k$ and midpoint $x_0$ to see the transition shape change.
reply.instructions: Move the sliders to change the steepness and midpoint of the curve. Observe how the output and tangent slope update in real time.
